historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2027-FY2029 average revenue growth, bracketed by the revenue 5yr CAGR (9.4%, FY2020 covid-trough base) and the equity 5yr CAGR (8.4%, depressed by $2.3B of buybacks). FY2026 guided growth of ~22% is acquisition-inflated and not a run-rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (8.4%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (44.4%) and owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (41.4%). Both are measured from the FY2020-22 covid trough (FY2020 FCF -$258M, FY2021 EPS $0.60) and are recovery arithmetic, not sustainable growth; equity is also held down by buybacks. Neither is used as the forward anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, company is net-debt): FY2022 464, FY2023 555, FY2024 865, FY2025 1,312. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (41.4%) is above the reported-FCF CAGR (38.4%): SBC + withholding grew slower than cash flow (76 -> 119, +16%/yr vs FCF +38%/yr), so stock comp is a shrinking share of cash generation, not a growing one. FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-304), so the 5yr FCF CAGR is undefined. EPS CAGRs use FY2020 NI/shares (0.59) as the 5yr base because the FY2020 EPS cell is blank.

scenario_narratives.base: Aerospace up-cycle matures; spares and IGT sustain ~8% mid-decade growth and ~2pp of margin expansion; GE/SpaceX insourcing costs some pricing power after 2030 but not the franchise. WACC 9%, terminal growth 3%, 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates, IGT and spares all keep compounding; margins reach 37.5% pre-SBC; insourcing stays a headline. Terminal growth 3.5%, 18x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Aerospace downcycle FY2028-30 plus real share loss to GE/SpaceX in-house casting after the 2030 contract roll; margins trough at 27.5% pre-SBC and recover to ~30%. Terminal growth 2.5%, 13x cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Howmet as a stream of unlevered owner free cash flow: company adjusted EBITDA restated pre-SBC, less SBC plus equity-award withholding, D&A, a cash tax rate ramping to 21%, a capex programme that peaks in 2027, and working capital that consumes 10% of each year's revenue growth. Three scenarios built on the company's actual axes (OEM build rates, IGT/data-centre demand, spares mix, and GE/SpaceX insourcing after the 2030 contract cycle), discounted at a single USD 9% WACC with cyclicality charged in the flows and weights rather than the discount rate. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and a 13-18x owner-FCF cap. The market price implies a terminal multiple and growth path well above the base case; the sensitivity grid and required-return table show what return today's price buys.
key_risks_to_valuation: GE Aerospace and SpaceX in-house turbine blade/vane casting eroding the highest-margin Engine Products franchise after long-term agreements expire around 2030
Commercial aerospace new-build downcycle (Boeing/Airbus rate cuts, engine OEM destocking) hitting ~70% of revenue
Data-centre power capex slowdown removing the industrial gas turbine tailwind that is driving current margin expansion
Customer concentration: GE Aerospace ~14% of third-party sales; a handful of OEMs drive volume
Premium multiple (~49x trailing P/E) means the equity is priced for the bull path; a 100bp change in WACC moves the base value materially
Debt-funded M&A (CAM $1.8B) raising net debt to ~$3.9B; integration risk in Fastening Systems
Titanium, rhenium and nickel superalloy supply from geopolitically sensitive sources
Forged Wheels exposure to Class 8 truck cyclicality

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 183.83-310.00
data_sources.financials: HWM_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts via the DB-first pipeline, millions USD): FY2025 10-K actuals for the base year, Q2 2026 10-Q for net debt and share count; kpis table for cash taxes, equity-award taxes, buybacks and interest income
data_sources.guidance: Q2 2026 earnings release / call (August 2026) as recorded in HWM_Analysis.json: FY2026 revenue $10.05B +/-$50M, adj EBITDA $3.23B +/-$20M, adj EPS $5.27, FCF $1.9B, capex >$500M rising in 2027
data_sources.qualitative: HWM_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): segments, moat, GE/SpaceX insourcing risk, CAM acquisition, bull/bear cases

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 402M shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover/balance sheet) plus ~3M dilutive RSUs/options (Q2 2026 diluted EPS 1.33 on NI 534 implies ~401.5M weighted diluted; end-of-period basic 402M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks (FY2025 $700M, H1 2026 $600M) fund the flat count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $73M plus $46M taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing). Howmet publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and does not add SBC back to adjusted EBITDA, so the two cash-flow lines are summed. Interest income ($20M FY2025) is NOT deducted: the company is net-debt (~$3.9B), so there is no cash pile being double-counted.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $700M; H1 2026 $600M (~$800M YTD at ~$248 average per the Q2 call). Repurchaser: the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% risk-free, 5.0% ERP, beta ~1.1 gives cost of equity ~9.7%; ~$4.5B debt at ~5.5% pre-tax (4.3% after tax) is ~5% of a ~$97B EV, so WACC rounds to 9.0%. Below the 10.5% US-tech house default because Howmet carries a multi-year OEM backlog, long-term supply agreements to 2030 and a 22%-of-revenue spares annuity; above a utility-grade rate because new-build volumes remain cyclical. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, GE/SpaceX insourcing and customer concentration are charged in the bear flows and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, so leases are treated as an operating cost (treatment B). Operating lease liabilities are excluded from total_debt (XBRL debt is borrowings only); finance leases are immaterial. No lease principal is separately deducted, so leases are charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: IMPORTANT for readers of ebitda_margin_path: Howmet's adjusted EBITDA (and the DB EBITDA = operating income + D&A) is AFTER stock-based compensation expense (FY2025 2,329 = 28.2%; FY2026 guide 3,230 = 32.1%). The engine deducts sbc_pct_path from EBITDA, so ebitda_margin_path is stated PRE-SBC (company adj EBITDA + SBC add-back: FY2025 29.1%, FY2026 ~33.0%). Net of the 1.4% SBC-plus-withholding charge the modelled FY2026 post-SBC margin is ~31.6%, i.e. guidance less the 0.5% cash cost of equity-award withholding. SBC is therefore charged once, not twice.
inputs.horizon_note: Ten-year explicit horizon, FY2026-FY2035, from FY2025 actuals. FY2026 is three-quarters elapsed and guided; it is treated as Y1 and discounted a full period (end-of-year convention, house rule), which is mildly conservative. Net debt is the 2026-06-30 balance, which already reflects H1 2026 FCF (~$838M) net of $600M buybacks and ~$100M dividends; the residual ~$140M (~$0.35/share) of H1 cash is counted twice, offset by the excess discounting of Y1. Both effects are immaterial and left as-is.
inputs.pension_note: Legacy Alcoa/Arconic pension and OPEB obligations are not added to net debt: ongoing contributions run through operating cash flow (inside the historical FCF and the modelled margins) and the plans have been substantially annuitised; the Analysis JSON rates the residual as low severity. Not verified against the FY2025 10-K pension note in this build.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Howmet is a profitable, growing engineered-products manufacturer (jet engine airfoils, aerospace fasteners, titanium/aluminium structures, forged truck wheels) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco features. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). Anchors: FY2025 10-K actuals for the base year; FY2026 guidance raised at Q2 2026 (revenue $10.05B, adj EBITDA $3.23B, FCF $1.9B, capex >$500M) for Y1; Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet for net debt and shares. CAM ($1.8B, closed April 2026) and Brunner are in both the FY2026 revenue guide (~$275M for ~9 months) and the June net debt; the remaining ~$95M annualisation is in FY2027 growth. Working capital: manufacturer with inventory + receivables > payables, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is negative (-10% of the revenue increase), calibrated so the modelled FY2026 unlevered owner FCF (~$1.96B) ties to the $1.9B levered FCF guide after ~$190M interest and ~$70M equity-award withholding. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes $312M were ~15% of EBIT (about 17% unlevered, excluding the interest shield); ramped to a 21% normal rate by FY2029.

bear.narrative: Bear: Y1 at the bottom of the guidance range ($10.0B) since three quarters are locked. FY2027 slows to +5% as Boeing rate increases stall and Class 8 truck volumes stay weak; FY2028-30 sees a classic aerospace downcycle (revenue -6%/-2%) with destocking at the engine OEMs, while data-centre capex decelerates and the IGT windfall fades. GE Aerospace (~14% of sales) and SpaceX bring meaningful airfoil casting in-house as the 2030 long-term agreements roll, taking volume and pricing from the highest-margin Engine Products line; pre-SBC margins trough at 27.5% (still above FY2023's ~24%) and recover only to ~30%. Capex is cut to maintenance. The business survives comfortably; the terminal value is capped at 13x owner FCF for a cyclical whose moat has been shown to be contestable.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2026 guidance midpoint $10.05B (+21.8%, incl. ~$275M CAM/Brunner). FY2027 +11%: ~10% organic (737 MAX 42/month and Airbus narrow-body rate rises, wide-body rates rising through 2027, IGT blades for data-centre power, spares +37% YoY) plus ~1% CAM annualisation. Decelerates 9->3% as the build-rate recovery matures and the installed-base annuity becomes the main driver.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC basis (see inputs.ebitda_basis_note). FY2026 33.0% pre-SBC = 32.1% guided post-SBC. Expands ~2pp on spares mix, price/cost and operating leverage, peaks at 35.0% FY2031-33, then fades 0.4pp into the terminal year as GE Aerospace/SpaceX in-house casting takes some Engine Products pricing power after the 2030 contract cycle.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 >$500M (5.2%), management flags a further rise in 2027 (6.0%) for engine-products and fastener capacity; normalises toward 4.0% (slightly above D&A of 3.8%) as the capacity build completes.
base.narrative: Base: the aerospace up-cycle runs its course. Narrow- and wide-body rates keep rising into 2028, IGT demand stays strong but decelerates, spares grow to ~25% of revenue, CAM integrates on plan. GE/SpaceX insourcing is real but slow and limited to specific parts; Howmet keeps the bulk of its airfoil franchise but loses some pricing leverage after 2030. Cash tax normalises to 21%, capex peaks in 2027 then fades.

bull.narrative: Bull: Y1 at the top of the guidance range ($10.1B). Boeing sustains 737 rate 47+ and 787 rate 10+, Airbus reaches A320 rate 75, and the data-centre power buildout keeps IGT blade demand 'extraordinary' into the 2030s where Howmet holds >50% share. Spares compound toward 30% of revenue, lifting margins to 37.5% pre-SBC. Defence (F-35, PAC-3, THAAD, Tomahawk) adds a second leg. Insourcing by GE/SpaceX proves technically slow and stays a headline rather than a share loss; long-term agreements are renewed at 2030. Bolt-on M&A (CAM-style) adds scale in fasteners.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates customer vertical integration as HIGH severity, and the largest customer (GE Aerospace, ~14% of sales) is simultaneously the emerging competitor, which is the single-customer-dependency trigger in the method; commercial aerospace has produced a real downcycle roughly once a decade. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs three independent things to hold at once (OEM rate increases delivered, data-centre IGT demand sustained, insourcing failing), and the stock already trades at ~49x trailing earnings, so the bull outcome is largely what the market price assumes.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
